messages:
Alex: Quick heads-up — I'll be handing off primary on-call to @Maria at 17:00 UTC today. Wanted to post a short shadowing plan for Lee (new hire) and a checklist for the handover. TL;DR: primary rotates, secondary stays Sam, APAC overnight has a coverage gap we should discuss.

Oncall-Bot: Scheduled rotation queued: Alex -> Maria @ 2026-03-14 17:00 UTC. Pager rules updated, reminder posted to #incidents.

Maria: Ack — I'll take primary at 17:00. @Lee welcome! can you shadow 17:00–19:00? we'll pair on any pages and I'll walk through the runbook. :pray:

Lee: Lee: happy to shadow, thanks. First time on-call for infra incidents — what's the fastest way to get set up?

Alex: Alex: short checklist for Lee before 17:00: 1) confirm PagerDuty login + MFA, 2) ssh access to jump host (ssh lee@jump.redwood.internal), 3) join #incidents and set DND off, 4) skim runbooks below. I added a desktop sticky with the key commands.

Sam: Sam: leaving a few runbook pointers here — if you get a P1 (service down) follow this minimal triage:

```
1) Run quick health check: curl -sS https://health.redwood.internal/ready
2) Check GPU pool: /ops/gpu-monitor ps -a
3) Rollback recent model rollout if latency spike correlates: infra runbook -> rollback section
4) Notify #incidents with impact + ETA
```

Sam: Sam: If you see repeated token-generation timeouts (>10% error rate) tag with "latency-regression" and ping @Jamie and @Taylor.

Jamie: Jamie: Note on escalation — if you get >2 high-latency pages within 10m escalate to infra on-call and open a dedicated incident channel (#incident-<ts>). Also: monitoring sometimes flaps when the cache node restarts — check KV-cache logs: /var/log/kvcache/kvcache.log.

Taylor: Taylor: APAC overnight coverage gap — we currently have no second for 00:00–06:00 UTC on weekends. If anyone can take on a recurring secondary shift for the east region please reply. We should avoid waking a PM unless it's service-impacting.

DevOps-Bot: DevOps-Bot: PagerDuty schedule snapshot:

```
Primary: Maria (2026-03-14T17:00Z -> 2026-03-15T09:00Z)
Secondary: Sam (on-call)
Shadow: Lee (17:00-19:00)
On-call rotation: weekly
```

Alex: Alex: quick handover pointers for Maria: 1) primary owns customer-impact comms, 2) use the "mitigate-first" playbook for transient latency, 3) prefer canary model fallback if serving runtime fails (runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/mitigate-model-failure).

Maria: Maria: got it. @Lee when we pair i'll show you how to: attach to the runner, tail logs, trigger a canary rollback. We'll test one simulated page before 18:00.

Lee: Lee: sounds great. Where's the simulated page script?

Alex: Alex: it's under ops/testing/simulate_page.sh — run with `./simulate_page.sh --type latency --env staging` first. Don't run against prod unless we coordinate.

Sam: Sam: also note: if PagerDuty notification fails (rare), we have manual escalation contact list in the runbook. Make sure your mobile is in PD.

Jamie: Jamie: small suggestion — new shadower checklist at top of runbook: login, ssh, PD test, join #incidents, test simulate script. I'll add it.

Maria: Maria: one more operational item — pair's expected to take the first 10m of any page and then hand back to primary once mitigated. If it becomes multi-team (infra+runtime) keep incident commander until we have a stable mitigation.

Alex: Alex: posting a short handoff snippet to paste into incident channel during the swap:

```
Handoff: Alex -> Maria | Primary active: Maria | Shadow: Lee (17:00-19:00) | Secondary: Sam
Key notes: APAC gap exists 00:00-06:00 UTC, runbook links: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/oncall and https://internal.redwood/runbooks/mitigate-model-failure
```

Taylor: Taylor: noted — tagging leadership for APAC coverage planning. @eng-leads can we get a follow-up in planning?

Maria: Maria: ready to take over. @Lee i'll DM credentials checklist in 15m and we'll pair up at 17:00. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
